name: rjd3nowcasting
what_it_holds: R interface to the JDemetra+ v3 (official EU statistical software) nowcasting engine: DFM specification/estimation and news-analysis functionality, GUI-inspired API from the JDemetra+ V2 nowcasting add-in used by some EU statistical agencies. Published by the rjdverse org (successor to EU/Bank of Belgium seasonal-adjustment tooling). EUPL-1.2 licensed, 152 commits, requires Java 21+.
why_useful: Production-grade DFM/news-analysis tooling used in official European statistics context; could be applied to Eurostat tour_ce_omr or EU consumer-confidence panels we already hold, to build a proper EU nights nowcast with news decomposition rather than ad hoc constructions.
themes: Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies
why_all: Production-grade DFM/news-analysis tooling used in official European statistics context; could be applied to Eurostat tour_ce_omr or EU consumer-confidence panels we already hold, to build a proper EU nights nowcast with news decomposition rather than ad hoc constructions.

name: wayback (EDGI)
what_it_holds: Python client library (977 commits, BSD-3-Clause) from the Environmental Data & Governance Initiative for finding/loading historical Wayback Machine captures of specific URLs; built for their environmental-page monitoring work but generic.
why_useful: Well-maintained alternative to waybackpy with a more research-oriented API (used in academic replication pipelines); same use case for gaps #1, #2, #17.
last_activity: unspecified, actively developed by an established org (EDGI)
themes: Wayback Machine / Internet Archive tooling and archived-page datasets (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA/Mashvisor market pages, archived Inside Airbnb site)
Airbnb corporate open source (airbnb org) and public data pipelines built on Airbnb-internal-style data; Airbnb Data Science blog notebooks; Airbnb Newsroom scrapers
why_all: Well-maintained alternative to waybackpy with a more research-oriented API (used in academic replication pipelines); same use case for gaps #1, #2, #17.

Same class as waybackpack above, more actively maintained (EDGI is a live project) — usable for pulling dated snapshots of newsroom.airbnb.com, ir.airbnb.com guidance pages, or third-party STR-data-vendor market pages (AirDNA, Key Data, etc.) for point-in-time reconstruction, directly serving gap #17.

name: cdx_toolkit
what_it_holds: Official Common Crawl org's Python toolkit for querying CDX indices (Common Crawl and Internet Archive Wayback). Pulls index rows and fetches WARC records by offset/length; no committed dataset, purely a client library/CLI. 211 stars, Apache-2.0, updated 7 Sep 2026 (actively maintained).
why_useful: This is almost certainly the tool underlying our existing Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (2.08M rows, 50 crawls) and the 3,000 WARC renders we already hold; documents how to re-pull or extend that index to more crawls, other domains (Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, competitor STR platforms), or historical date ranges for the same host — directly extends gap targets 9 (competitor supply) and 17 (methods).
duplicate_of_holding: We already hold a CC CDX index over airbnb.com and WARC renders; this is the generating tool, not new data
themes: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: This is almost certainly the tool underlying our existing Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (2.08M rows, 50 crawls) and the 3,000 WARC renders we already hold; documents how to re-pull or extend that index to more crawls, other domains (Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, competitor STR platforms), or historical date ranges for the same host — directly extends gap targets 9 (competitor supply) and 17 (methods).

name: warcio
what_it_holds: Streaming WARC/ARC record reader/writer library (Python), used to parse the WARC files that cdx_toolkit or direct CC fetches return. 472 stars, Apache-2.0, updated 8 Sep 2026, actively maintained by the Webrecorder/Internet Archive-adjacent team.
why_useful: Needed to actually read the 3,000 WARC renders we already captured, or any new WARC pulls for competitor sites (Vrbo, Sonder, Vacasa, Hipcamp listing pages) to extract page text/prices/counts at a point in time.
themes: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: Needed to actually read the 3,000 WARC renders we already captured, or any new WARC pulls for competitor sites (Vrbo, Sonder, Vacasa, Hipcamp listing pages) to extract page text/prices/counts at a point in time.

Needed to actually open/parse the 3,000 WARC renders we already captured (or any new ones pulled via cdx_toolkit) without standing up Spark; low-friction way to extract page text/HTML from archived Airbnb, AirDNA, or competitor pages for point-in-time price/availability text mining.

name: arrhivescrape
what_it_holds: Reusable Wayback Machine / CDX-based static-site recovery toolkit with a CLI and local web UI, for reconstructing archived versions of a site from CDX index entries. 0 stars, no license, updated 26 Jun 2026.
why_useful: Matches gap 17's 'Wayback Machine tooling (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA market pages)' — could be pointed (with human sign-off, not run by an agent) at archived AirDNA market pages or historical airbnb.com pages already indexed by CDX to reconstruct point-in-time snapshots.
